name: tradingcalc
description: Trading math tools: Black-Scholes and options payoff, forex position size and pip value, VaR and Sharpe, plus crypto futures PnL and liquidation. Deterministic: the same inputs always return the same outputs.

interface.longDescription:
TradingCalc is a set of read-only calculators for trading math. The same inputs always return the same outputs.

Options: Black-Scholes price and Greeks, payoff and breakeven, straddle and strangle, covered call and protective put, implied volatility.

Forex: position size from a risk budget, pip value, margin, swap cost, currency conversion and pair correlation, with live rates for the account currency.

Risk and statistics: VaR and expected shortfall, Sharpe ratio, deflated Sharpe, Kelly sizing, GARCH volatility, risk parity, portfolio tearsheet.

Crypto futures: PnL, liquidation price, breakeven, funding cost, position size, for linear and coin-margined contracts.

Also on-chain token and wallet checks. Nothing you enter is stored. The core formulas are checked against public test vectors at https://tradingcalc.io/verify.
defaultPrompt: I have $10,000 and want to risk 1% on a BTC long at 83,000 with a stop at 81,500. What position size is that?
Price a BTC call, strike 90,000, 30 days to expiry, 55% volatility, and show the Greeks.
What does a 0.5 lot EUR/USD position risk in dollars with a 30 pip stop?

positive.description: Position size from a risk budget, linear futures
positive.prompt: I want to go long BTC/USDT at 83,000 with a stop at 81,500, risking 100 USDT at 5x leverage. What position size is that?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a size of about 0.0642 BTC (about 5,330 USDT notional), margin about 1,066 USDT and a stop distance of about 1.81 percent. The numbers come from the tool, not from the model.

positive.description: Black-Scholes price and Greeks for a BTC option
positive.prompt: Price a BTC call with spot 84,000, strike 90,000, 30 days to expiry and 55 percent volatility, and show the Greeks.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a call price of about 2,981 USD and a put price of about 8,981 USD at zero interest, call delta about 0.36, with gamma, vega and theta in the same result.

positive.description: Forex position size in the account currency
positive.prompt: I have a USD account. I want to buy EUR/USD at 1.0850 with a stop at 1.0820 and risk 200 USD. How many lots?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a stop distance of 30 pips, 66,667 units (about 0.67 standard lots) for a 200 USD risk, with USD as the account currency.

positive.description: Liquidation price of a leveraged long
positive.prompt: Where is the liquidation price of a BTC long entered at 83,000 with 10x leverage, linear contract?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a liquidation price of 75,115 for the isolated linear formula stated in the tool description.

positive.description: Parametric VaR and CVaR from a return series
positive.expected_behavior: Returns parametric normal VaR of about 2.46 percent and CVaR of about 3.06 percent from 20 observations, with skewness and a modified VaR of about 2.66 percent.

negative.description: A price prediction or buy signal request: the plugin only calculates from numbers the user gives, it does not forecast
negative.prompt: Which coin will go up the most next week? Give me a buy signal for BTC or ETH.

negative.description: An order or transfer request: the plugin is read-only and cannot place trades or move funds
negative.prompt: Buy 0.5 BTC on Binance for me right now and move 1,000 USDT from my wallet to my exchange account.

negative.description: Non-trading math that sounds like a calculator request: loans and taxes are out of scope
negative.prompt: Calculate the monthly payment on a 300,000 dollar mortgage at 6.5 percent over 30 years.

publication.release_notes: Read-only trading math calculators: options, forex, risk and statistics, crypto futures. The same inputs always return the same outputs.
